subject.title: fix(sms): isolate validated webhook quotas per sender

question: Should validated SMS callbacks retain a bounded aggregate account-and-route admission cap in addition to the new per-sender quota, and what ceiling should protect durable ingress without recreating shared-egress cross-throttling?
rationale: The branch intentionally removes the previous shared dispatch ceiling, while the bounded-key limiter only caps retained state. Selecting the aggregate capacity contract is a product and operational policy decision, not a mechanical refactor choice.

options.title: Add a bounded aggregate validated cap
options.body: Keep the canonical per-sender 30/minute fairness limit and add a post-validation account-and-route aggregate ceiling with fan-out and overload tests.

options.title: Accept unbounded sender fan-out
options.body: Merge the per-sender-only policy and explicitly accept that valid traffic from many senders may consume substantially more ingress capacity than before.

recommendation.title: Add a bounded aggregate validated cap
recommendation.body: Keep the canonical per-sender 30/minute fairness limit and add a post-validation account-and-route aggregate ceiling with fan-out and overload tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the identified recent contributor to the current-main Twilio RCS sender-normalization path that this quota design extends.
